claim: The U.S. Department of Justice's Epstein file production contains anonymous, uncorroborated submissions alleging that two girls were buried at Zorro Ranch, Epstein's roughly-10,000-acre property near Stanley, New Mexico. One is a November 2019 email forwarded into the case file from a sender claiming to be "former staff at the Zorro," asserting that "two foreign girls were buried" in the hills outside the ranch and offering purported video material. Another appears in an FBI crisis-intake tip serial in which an anonymous source offers "the location of two foreign girls buried on Zorro Ranch" together with abuse videos "for sale for one bitcoin." These are unverified tip and apparent extortion materials captured in the investigative file, not findings: no body recovery, excavation result, or charge corroborates them. In Epstein staff's own operational emails, the phrase "leave them at Zorro" refers to shipping containers and vehicles ("Unless you want to use our container and leave them at Zorro than it wouldn't make sense to send our containers"). The submissions are primary records that exist in the release; their allegations remain uncorroborated.

EFTA01684300 is an FBI serial index (FD-302 / 'Crisis Intak' entries, correspondence to Director Wray) logging an anonymous source ('ANON') offering videos + the burial 'location' for one bitcoin. Neither is a finding; presented as on-the-record-but-uncorroborated per the project's attribute-don't-adopt rule.
